title: Does Vinyl Plank Need a Moisture Test Over Concrete?
meta: Vinyl plank over concrete needs a moisture test if it is glued down or the warranty says so; floating rigid core is more forgiving. Wills Flooring, Kirkland.
keywords: vinyl plank moisture test concrete, concrete moisture test before flooring, LVP over concrete slab, calcium chloride test vinyl plank, vinyl plank basement Kirkland

blocks.lead: Yes, if the plank is glued down, and yes if the manufacturer's warranty requires it, which most do. A floating rigid-core plank over a slab is far more forgiving, but we still test, because the plank is waterproof and the glue, the underlayment and the subfloor under it are not.
blocks.detail: The plank does not care about moisture. What fails is the adhesive, the mold that grows under a floating floor, and the warranty claim you file afterward. A test takes an afternoon and costs less than any of those.

blocks.html: Kirkland is a slab town more than people realize. Daylight basements on the Finn Hill and Juanita slopes, walk-out lower levels on the lake side of Houghton, Totem Lake condos built on grade, and every garage conversion in Rose Hill sit on concrete. Vinyl plank is the floor most of them get. Whether it needs a moisture test is a question we answer at nearly every one of those estimates, and the honest answer has three parts: what the plank needs, what the warranty needs, and what your slab is actually doing.

blocks.text: What the moisture is doing under the plank

items.title: Concrete never fully dries
items.text: A slab poured in 1978 still pulls water vapor up from the soil. Without a vapor barrier beneath it, and many older Kirkland slabs have none or a torn one, that vapor moves up through the concrete and stops at whatever you put on top.

items.title: Glue fails first
items.text: Glue-down vinyl uses a pressure-sensitive adhesive that turns back to liquid under sustained moisture. The planks slide, gap and lift at the edges. This is the failure a moisture test exists to prevent.

items.title: Floating floors trap it
items.text: A floating rigid-core plank does not fail, but the vapor collects under it. Over a year that means a musty lower level and, on a damp slab, mold on the underside of the underlayment. The plank looks perfect while the room smells wrong.

items.title: The warranty reads the number
items.text: Nearly every vinyl plank warranty lists a maximum slab moisture level. If you file a claim and there is no test on record, the claim is denied. A test protects you as much as the floor.

blocks.text: The three tests, and which one you actually need

head: Test
What it measures
When we use it
rows: Relative moisture near the surface, in minutes
Every estimate on a slab. A screening tool, not a warranty document.
Whether vapor condenses under taped plastic in 16 to 72 hours
Quick yes-or-no on a suspect slab. Cheap, and you can do it yourself.
RH inside the slab at 40 percent of its depth, after 24 hours
Glue-down installs and any job where the manufacturer's warranty names a limit. This is the number the warranty wants.
Vapor emission in pounds per 1,000 sq ft per 24 hours
Older standard, still named in some warranties. Less reliable on slabs that have been heated or recently cleaned.
blocks.note: Common warranty limits are around 75 to 80 percent RH for glue-down, higher for floating rigid core. We check your specific plank's spec sheet, not a rule of thumb.

blocks.text: What happens when a Kirkland slab tests high

items.text: A high reading on one wall usually means a downspout, a clogged footing drain or grading that slopes toward the house. Fixing that outside is cheaper than anything we do inside.
items.note: Lake-side and hillside lots in Juanita and Houghton are the usual suspects

items.text: If glue-down was the plan and the slab is borderline, a floating SPC plank over a vapor-retarding underlayment removes the adhesive from the equation.
items.note: Same $2.50 per sq ft labor either way

items.text: For slabs that stay high, an epoxy vapor retarder rolled onto the concrete blocks vapor at the source. This is the fix for a finished lower level you cannot dig around.
items.note: Quoted at the estimate; adds a day for cure

items.text: A retest after mitigation goes in the file with the warranty registration. Then the floor goes down like any other vinyl plank job, usually one to two days for a lower level.
items.note: Example: 700 sq ft lower level × $2.50 = $1,750 labor

blocks.text: When you can skip the lab test, honestly

a.title: A quick meter check is enough when
items: Floating rigid-core plank over a vapor-retarding underlayment
The slab is above grade, such as a Totem Lake condo on a podium
The room has been finished for years with no odor, stains or peeling paint at the base of walls
The plank warranty does not name an RH or emission limit for floating installs

b.title: Do the probe test when
items: Below-grade rooms on a hillside or lake lot
The slab was poured in the last year, which is common in Kirkland ADUs and garage conversions
You see efflorescence, dark patches, or old carpet tack strip that rusted
You want the warranty to hold up

blocks.title: The mistake we see most in Kirkland lower levels:
blocks.text: Someone reads that rigid-core vinyl is waterproof, skips the test, floats it straight on the slab with a foam pad that has no vapor barrier, and calls us 18 months later about a smell. The plank was fine. The pad was black underneath. Waterproof describes the plank, not the room. Learn more about what waterproof actually means for vinyl plank.
Checklist before vinyl plank goes on your slab

items.html: Ask the installer how they test. If the answer is "we look at it," keep looking. We meter every slab at the free estimate and recommend probes when the numbers or the install method call for it.
Read the plank's installation guide, not the box. The moisture limit and the required underlayment are in the install guide. The box says waterproof.
Use an underlayment with a built-in vapor barrier on any floating install over concrete, even when the slab tests fine. It is cheap insurance and most warranties require it.
Flatten before you worry about moisture. Older Kirkland slabs have humps and cracks. A plank over a high spot fails at the joint no matter how dry the slab is. Flattening is quoted at the estimate.
Fix the outside first. Gutters, downspout extensions and grading solve more wet-slab problems than any product we can put down.

Keep the test results. Wills Flooring records the readings on your quote and covers the install with a 1-year workmanship warranty. That paperwork is what makes the plank manufacturer's warranty real. See our vinyl plank installation page for what is included.

faq.q: How much does a concrete moisture test cost?
faq.a: A meter reading is part of every free Wills Flooring estimate on a slab. If the readings or a glue-down install call for in-situ probes, that lab-grade test is quoted with the job. Either way it is a small line next to the floor itself, and it protects the manufacturer's warranty.

faq.q: Can I do a moisture test on concrete myself?
faq.a: Yes. Tape a two-foot square of clear plastic to the slab on all four edges and leave it 24 to 72 hours. Condensation or a dark patch under the plastic means vapor is coming through and a proper test is needed. A dry sheet is encouraging but not a warranty document.

faq.q: Is rigid-core vinyl plank really fine over a damp basement slab?
faq.a: The plank is. The room is not. Vapor still rises and sits under the floor, so you need a vapor-retarding underlayment and, on a slab that tests high, a mitigation coating. Skipping both is how a Kirkland lower level ends up with a musty smell over a perfect-looking floor.

faq.q: Do I need a vapor barrier under vinyl plank on concrete?
faq.a: For a floating install, use an underlayment with an attached vapor barrier or a separate 6 mil poly sheet, unless the plank has one built in. For glue-down, the adhesive and slab reading do the work, and a mitigation coating replaces the barrier when readings are high.

faq.q: How long does a new slab need to cure before vinyl plank?
faq.a: Roughly one month per inch of thickness as a rule of thumb, so a 4-inch ADU or garage-conversion slab wants 60 to 90 days before testing. New slabs almost always test high early. Test, wait, retest, then install.

faq.q: What if my slab tests high and I do not want to wait?
faq.a: A moisture mitigation coating lets us install within a couple of days on a high-reading slab. It is a real cost, so we quote it only when the readings and the plank warranty require it. On a borderline slab, switching from glue-down to floating rigid core is often enough.
